This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 26.04.2022 at about 3.30 p.m. she was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KJ4284 infront Royal Enfield Showroom, Hosur Bengaluru NH44 Service Road, Bommasandra, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time, car bearing Reg.No.AP03BD0345 driver by its driver rashly and negligently and dashed against her, due to the said impact, she fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Sparsha Hospital, wherein she took treatment as indoor patient, for which she has spent an SCCH5 amount of Rs.1,50,000/ towards hospitalization and medicine.

3. At the time of the accident, she was aged about 27 years, hale and healthy, working in private company, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., due to this accident she is suffering from lot of physical and mental stress torture and frustration.
She has also lost her earnings.

Out of this accident crime No.114/2022 is registered against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.AP03BD 0345 before the Hebbagodi Police Station for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 owner of the said car , they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH5 4.
On service of notice, Respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed his written statement and denied the averments of the petition.

He has denied issuance of insurance policy to the car bearing Reshma R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126632437/
2 Reg.No.AP03BD 0345.

Further stated that, petitioner has ridden her motor cycle without driving license and without wearing helmet in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car bearing Reg.No.AP03BD 0345.
Further stated that, there is lapse of 3 days in lodging the complaint.
Respondent No.1 has denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence her petition is not SCCH5 maintainable.

R2/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 26.04.2022 at about 3.30 p.m. when she was proceeding in her motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KJ4284 infront of Royal Enfield Showroom, Bommasandra, Anekal Taluk, Hosur, Bengaluru at that time, Car bearing Reg.No.AP03BD0345 in a rash and negligent riding dashed to the petitioner motor cycle and caused the accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
SCCH5 3.
Whether the owner of the offending vehicle has discharged his initial burden by way of producing relevant documents?
4. What order or award?

On the other hand, MRO, Sparsha Hospital is examined as RW1, AO of respondent No.1 company is examined as RW2 and marked 5 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5 and closed his evidence.

8. Issue No.1:
In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In support of her case, she exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is SCCH5 marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.6.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, she examined one Doctor as PW2.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW2 and her records which was marked as FIR, complaint, mahazar,
seizure mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 26.04.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW1.
10.

On the other hand, MRO of Sparsha Hospital is examined as RW1 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1, copy of MLC register marked as Ex.R.2, copy of Police Intimation marked as Ex.R.3.

Further AO of respondent No.1 is examined as RW2 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.4 and copy of statement marked as Ex.R.5.
SCCH5 11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement and oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about noncausing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 26.04.2022 at about 3.30 p.m. she was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA 05KJ4284 infront Royal Enfield Showroom, Hosur Bengaluru NH44 Service Road,
Bommasandra, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such SCCH5 circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained left distal radius fracture extending into the distal 1/3rd shaft.

To prove the said fact, she has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary issued by Sparsha Hospital marked as Ex.P.9 wherein she took treatment as indoor patient from 26.04.2022 to 28.04.2022, medical bills marked as Ex.P.10 to the tune of Rs.68,206/, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.11, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.12, outpatient record marked as Ex.P.13.
SCCH5 14.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sparsha Hospital is examined as PW2 and furnished clinical notes marked as Ex.P.14, case sheet marked as Ex.P.15 and Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
PW2 has assessed total disability of the left arm at the rate of 35% and whole body disability at 12%.
In crossexamination he has categorically admitted that, he was one of the team member who has treated the petitioner.
Further he has deposed that, now the fracture is united and there is no complications at the fracture sight and petitioner can do her daytoday work with some difficulty.
PW2 Doctor has given assessment of disability i.e., total disability of the left arm at the rate of 35% and whole body disability at the rate of 12%.
So considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, functional disability SCCH5 is assessed at the rate of 10% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 27 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of driving licence marked as Ex.P.7, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 14.10.1994 and the alleged accident is occurred on 26.04.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.7 age of the petitioner is considered about 28 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 16. Further in the petition, petitioner has categorically stated that, prior to the accident she was hale and healthy and she was working in private SCCH5 company thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
To substantiate the said fact, she has not placed any documentary evidence.
In the absence of documentary evidence, I have no hesitation to disbelieve the case of the petitioner on the fact about occupation is concerned.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/ p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Further admittedly for incurring the expenses towards medical treatment, petitioner has marked Ex.P.10 medial bills.
As per the said document, she has spent Rs.68,206/ for the grievous injury sustained by her in Sparsha Hospital.
Contrary to the said fact, except denial in oral evidence of RW1 and RW2, they have not disproved the petitioner case.

So in the absence of iota of evidence,
I have no hesitation to accept the case of the petitioner with regard to entitlement of medical expenses, as she has spent an amount of Rs.68,206/ as per Ex.P.10 medical bills.
Hence petitioner is entitled for compensation for the said bills.

20 . Further admittedly as per the wound certificate and medical records, petitioner has suffered injuries caused in the accident and for the said pain and sufferings, conveyance, nourishment and attendant SCCH5 charges, she is entitled for compensation including for loss of amenities in her life, when she was admitted in the hospital.
Accordingly she is entitled for compensation for the said bills.

21. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of future income 3,00,90000 2. Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 68,206.00 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6. Loss of income during laid up 98300 period Total 4,15,08900 22.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,15,089/ with SCCH5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0516023121p103923875 which is valid for the period from 28.07.2021 to 27.07.2022, the alleged Reshma R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126632437/

: Under the facts and circumstances of the case, this issue is not proper.

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,15,089/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Fifteen Thousand Eighty Nine Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along SCCH5 with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
